Shertz Municipal Court is a city trial court house in the County of Guadalupe and is situated in the Municipal Complex of Hal Baldwin. It was established in Guadalupe Courthouse Square in 1855. It has jurisdiction over offenses in the city, including traffic and vehicle matters, criminal cases, city ordinances and State statute violations. Court rules are followed by everyone that visits the court.

How to search for the case record?

Shertz Municipal Court records are available online, in the county clerks and the county district offices. They can be found online by using the following ways:

  • Searching by name
  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by address
  • Searching by phone
  • Searching by email

Some recorded information about cases is not available online because they are lawfully confidential. These types of information are only available at the county court or district office. They can be obtained by giving an Open Public Records Request. Fill in all the information on the form, tell why you want this information, and pay the fees. The court will respond with whether to give this information or not. For more information about the public records, call or mail the court.

How can a person pay using the online system?

Shertz Municipal Court online payment can be made through the online portal of https://www.municipalonlinepayments.com/schertztx/court/search. Online payment can be made in three ways. The result will give you the violation type and the amount to be paid. Then you can pay with any online method. The three ways are:

Name

Payment can be made by entering the first and last name of the person with the date of birth.

Citation Number

Payment can be made by entering the citation number and birth date.

Driver’s License

Payment can be made by entering the driver’s license number with the state and date of birth.

When will the warrant be issued?

Shertz Municipal Court issued a warrant if a person did not pay fines on time, did not appear on the citation or summons and failed to obey the court's order. If a warrant is issued against you that your driver’s license will be suspended or denied for renewal according to the Texas Transportation Code under the Failure to Appear Program Chapter 706. You will be arrested if the court gives the order. If you pay the fine, your driver’s license will be renewed, and your arrest warrant will be suspended. Contact the warrant division for any information.

How to make a plea by mail?

Shertz Municipal Court plea can be sent through the mail. Two types of plea can be written and sent to court. The types are:

Plea of Guilty

If you are guilty or want to request a defensive driving or deferred disposition, write a guilty plea and send it to the court. The judge will give you a fine that you must pay on time. After taking the course, your cases can be removed from the records.

Plea of Not Guilty

If you do not feel guilty, write a plea of not guilty and send it to the court. You had to post a surety bond or cash to secure another court date. The judge will see all the facts and evidence and give you a schedule; you must appear in court on the date. You cannot request a defensive driving or deferred disposition in this case.

At the end of the form, write the date and your signature and mail it or go to the court in person.

How to make payments?

Shertz Municipal Court payments for fines can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the counter. Convenience and other charges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card. Payment plans are also available by this court. You can pay in installments or pay fully at once.

Online

A person can pay online using the New Jersey online payment link: https://www.municipalonlinepayments.com/schertztx/court/search. Service fees will be applied in this method. Defensive driving, dismissal, or deferred disposition request cannot be made if you pay online.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address. The address is 1400 Schertz Pkwy, Schertz, TX 78154, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted.

Which court rules must be followed in the court?

Shertz Municipal Court rules that must be followed by everyone that visits the court are:

  • Dress properly and appropriately. Do not wear tight, sleeveless and torn clothes. Hats, caps and sunglasses should be taken off during the court hearing.
  • Do not talk in court. Only speak when the judge asks something or addresses you.
  • Knives, any tools or sharp objects are prohibited in the court.
  • No eatables items are allowed in the court. Leave them before you enter the court.
  • No electronic devices are allowed. Cell phones are allowed but should be in silent mode or switched off.

How to represent yourself in court if you are involved in any case?

If you are involved in any case, you must represent yourself in court. You can hire a professional attorney or lawyer. The court proceedings are complex, and a skilled person with experience in that field will help you and represent you during the case hearing; if you want to fight the case by yourself, read the guidelines of self-represented litigants.

What to Expect in Court

If you've been charged with a Class C misdemeanor or a traffic offense in Shertz, you will receive a citation with a court date and time. On your court date, you will need to show up at the Shertz Municipal Court building, located at 1400 Schertz Parkway, Schertz, TX 78154.

When you arrive, you will need to check in with the court clerk and wait for your case to be called. The judge will read the charges against you and ask how you plead. You have the option to plead guilty, not guilty, or no contest.

If you plead guilty or no contest, the judge will sentence you on the spot. If you plead not guilty, your case will be set for a trial at a later date.

Your Options If You've Been Charged with a Crime

If you've been charged with a crime in Shertz, you have several options. You can plead guilty, no contest, or not guilty. If you plead guilty or no contest, you will be sentenced by the judge. If you plead not guilty, you have the right to a trial.

Before you make a decision, it's important to understand the consequences of each option. If you plead guilty or no contest, you will be convicted of the crime and it will go on your record. This could have serious consequences, such as a fine, jail time, or the loss of your driver's license.

If you plead not guilty and are found guilty at trial, you will also be convicted and face the same consequences as if you had pleaded guilty. However, if you are found not guilty at trial, you will not be convicted and the charges against you will be dismissed.

Hiring an Attorney

If you've been charged with a crime in Shertz, it's always a good idea to hire an attorney. An experienced attorney can help you understand your options and make the best decision for your situation. They can also represent you in court and help you navigate the legal system.

FAQ:

What is the phone number of the warrant division for this court?

Shertz Municipal Court warrant division phone number is 210-619-1663 or 210-619-1664.

I am financially weak and cannot pay the fine; what can I do?

Contact the court before the hiring date. Present all the documents to the court that prove you are financially weak and cannot pay fines.

What happens if I don’t pay the fine on time and do not appear in court?

If I don’t pay the fine on time and do not appear in court on the date written on the citation, then extra fines will be given, the license will be suspended, and sometimes a warranty against you will be issued.
